0.0.n: 中 adds the sense of throughout or all of something.

0.1.n: Marks 世界中 as the one doing the hating.

0.2.n: A very casual, often masculine address that can sound rough or intimate depending on the relationship.

0.3.n: Marks お前 as the person receiving the hatred.

0.4.n: The て-form of 嫌う connects to も to express an even-if condition.

0.5.n: After a verb’s て-form, も introduces a condition that will not change the outcome.

0.7.n: A strongly casual, typically masculine way to refer to yourself.

0.8.n: Sets 俺 apart from the world: others may hate you, but I will stay.

0.9.n: Refers to the space next to someone; whose side is understood from context.

0.10.n: Marks 隣 as the location where the speaker will be.

0.11.n: Used for a living person’s presence; its plain form can describe the present or future.

0.12.n: At the end of this promise, から gives reassuring grounds for an unspoken message such as don’t worry.

1.0.n: 恋 specifically refers to romantic feelings rather than love in every sense.

1.1.n: Marks 恋 as what the speakers do not know.

1.2.n: The plain negative form of 知る modifies 僕たち, describing which people are meant.

1.3.n: A typically masculine self-reference, gentler than 俺; here it combines with たち.

1.4.n: Attached to 僕, this suffix forms 僕たち, referring to the speaker and their group.

1.5.n: Marks the whole phrase 恋を知らない僕たち as the topic, leaving the statement unfinished.

2.0.n: The speaker names himself casually, leaving out a topic particle such as は.

2.2.n: Refers back to the speaker, 俺, rather than to another person.

2.3.n: Marks 自分 as the person being lied to.

2.4.n: Pairs with つく in the expression 嘘をつく; を is omitted in this casual speech.

2.5.n: With 嘘, つく means telling a lie, not physically making or attaching something.

2.6.n: Turns 自分に嘘つく into an activity that can be stopped; the following を is omitted.

2.7.n: The plain form of やめる expresses the speaker’s decision here, without a separate future ending.

0.lit: Even if the whole world hates you, as for me, because I will be beside you.
0.tip: A verb’s て-form plus も means even if, emphasizing that the speaker’s support will not change.

1.lit: As for us who do not know romantic love…
1.tip: The description 知らない comes before 僕たち; the final は leaves this title deliberately unfinished.

2.lit: I, to myself, telling lies—the act of it—I will stop.
2.tip: A verb phrase plus のやめる means stopping that activity; casual speech leaves out を before やめる.
